rationale: C10 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child: it was dated the same day, concerned the same Iranian oil settlement, and used closely parallel language about the oil problem, a valuable personal contribution, a successful solution, and the settlement's broader benefits. The child adapts this material from congratulations to the Shah into appreciation for Ambassador Henderson. C18 is the strongest structural alternative because it praises an official's personal qualities and contribution to a successful foreign-policy achievement, while C09 provides a similar Eisenhower gratitude-letter frame but less event-specific language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the splendid results of your work on the oil problem in Iran
shared_material.parent_excerpt: has reached, in principle, a fair and equitable settlement to the difficult oil problem
shared_material.explanation: Both identify the same Iranian oil problem and celebrate its successful resolution.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Your knowledge of the situation, your resourcefulness, your judgment and your tireless patience ... contributed greatly
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the negotiations to which you personally have made a valuable contribution
shared_material.explanation: Both attribute the settlement materially to the recipient's personal contribution.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The present solution of the Anglo-Iranian oil dispute ... is a major achievement
shared_material.parent_excerpt: we are happy to have helped in finding a solution to the oil problem
shared_material.explanation: The child closely reuses the solution-to-the-oil-problem formulation while recasting it as direct praise.

shared_material.child_excerpt: will not only further our objectives in the Middle East but also contribute to our good relations with our European allies
shared_material.parent_excerpt: implementation of this agreement ... will mark the beginning of a new era of economic progress and stability for your country
shared_material.explanation: Each moves from announcing the settlement to explaining its broader diplomatic or stabilizing consequences.
